newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK pension plan to hold 30 pct HK assets - paper.
newsitem.headline: HK pension plan to hold 30 pct HK assets - paper.

text.p: Proposed regulations for Hong Kong's Mandatory Provident Fund scheme show the government intends 30 percent of funds to be denominated in Hong Kong assets, the South China Morning Post said on Wednesday.

Citing a confidential draft of the scheme's proposed regulations, the newspaper said foreign currency exposure would be limited to 70 percent. It said the government had previously discussed a local exposure level of 50 percent.

Government officials are expected to meet with industry representatives next week for final consultations, it added. The South China Morning Post said current proposals would prevent schemes from holding more than 10 percent of any class of security issued by any single issuer.
Restrictions would also be placed on funds borrowing and bonds and debt securities would be restricted to government debt in Hong Kong or triple A-rated debt from outside Hong Kong.

The newspaper said investment in equities would be allowed only in fully paid-up shares listed on 32 recognised exchanges and the use of warrants would be restricted to five percent of the fund's assets. "Derivatives use will be restricted to hedging existing positions in a portfolio...and tactical asset allocation. In such cases, it will be restricted to 10 percent of the effective exposure of the fund," the South China Morning Post said.

It said companies would have to be incorporated in Hong Kong, registered with the Securities and Futures Commission and have capital and net assets of at least HK$10 million to qualify as fund managers for the scheme.
